Full Qoyod regression suite: 188 passed + 1 skipped (the prior /openapi.json catch-all skip from iter-256) across 10 test files — NO regression. New live HTTP smoke (test_qoyod_migration_last_order_date_iter257.py, 8/8 PASS) hits the public REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL with admin@hesab.app and confirms: GET /migration/products?sort=last_order_date&sort_dir=desc (rows sorted desc), GET /migration/products?last_order_after=2025-01-01 (rows filtered), same on /customers, both export.csv files include 'last_order_date' as a header column, and an invalid sort key (?sort=bogus) is rejected with 422 by FastAPI's regex Query validator. Frontend page renders correctly with all 5 new testids (sort-last-order-date on both tabs, filter-last-order-after-products, filter-last-order-after-customers, per-row last-order-date-{kind}-{i}) and Arabic header 'آخر طلب' visible; sort toggle and date filter both function. critical_code_review_comments: migration_routes.py:76 — Query(..., regex=...) is deprecated in FastAPI/Pydantic v2 in favour of `pattern=...`. Both still work, but the deprecation warning will eventually become an error; consider switching to pattern=^(occurrences|last_order_date|status)$.

migration_routes.py:88-90 — last_order_after compares as a STRING ($gte). This works only because last_order_date is stored as an ISO 'YYYY-MM-DD' or 'YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS+00:00' lexically-sortable string. Adding a tiny isoformat-validation (e.g. datetime.fromisoformat) would shield against bogus inputs like '2025/01/01' silently degrading to a no-op filter. Cosmetic.

migration.py:262 — best_date is compared with `>` between strings of mixed lengths ('2026-03-22' vs '2026-03-22T00:00:00+00:00'). They sort correctly in practice because the date prefix matches, but if a future code path inserts a non-UTC offset (e.g. '2026-03-21T23:00:00-01:00'), string compare will mis-rank. Consider normalising to a date-only prefix before max.

migration.py:236 — order_dates dict is built unbounded for all unified_orders of the tenant; on a 200k-order merchant this can spike memory by 30-50MB. Switch to a streaming cursor with projection-only fields or chunk by date range. Same concern noted in iter-256 for extract_mezan_customers — still no length cap.
Matching policy CONFIRMED still locked: test_last_order_date_does_not_change_mapping_decision passes — date does not influence auto_mapped vs candidate_match vs unmapped. ✔
